findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-argument version
findings.body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (lines 145-147) and immediately after another with signature `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (lines 149-151). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-positional-argument form is dead code and no longer callable. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. thumbnail generation code) that still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts)` will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because the method only accepts 2 positional args plus opts. This is a breaking API change that is easy to miss since Ruby only emits a silent 'method redefined' warning.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB upload size replaces configurable site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing admins to configure separate size limits for images vs. attachments. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types, so the `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` site settings are silently ignored on the client side. This creates an inconsistency with the server, which still reads `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` in `uploads_controller.rb` for the new downsizing feature, meaning client-side validation no longer matches server-side behavior for sites that configure a limit different from 10MB.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB value in displayErrorForUpload loses configured max_image_size_kb
findings.body: `displayErrorForUpload` previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to show the correct configured limit in the 413 error message. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB, so the error message shown to users will be wrong whenever an admin configures a different `max_image_size_kb` value, misleading users about the actual upload limit.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap for API URL uploads ignores max_image_size_kb setting
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was changed to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This removes respect for the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` setting when downloading images via API URL, allowing files up to 10MB regardless of the configured limit. While the new downsizing logic will later try to shrink the file, this silently changes the download-time cap for all sites, including those that intentionally set a stricter limit, and is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` elsewhere (e.g. `migrate_to_new_scheme`).

findings.title: In-place downsizing writes output over the same file being read, risking corruption
findings.body: The downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, using the same path for both source and destination. Image tools such as ImageMagick's `convert` and `gifsicle` are not guaranteed to be safe when input and output paths are identical — depending on how they open/truncate the output file, this can corrupt or truncate the file mid-read, especially for multi-frame/animated GIFs processed via gifsicle. This can result in a corrupted or zero-byte image being uploaded instead of a properly downsized one, with no validation afterward to catch this failure mode.

findings.title: Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, allowing silent failures and oversized uploads
findings.body: The loop `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its boolean return value (it returns false on failure, e.g. ImageMagick exits non-zero). If downsizing fails, the loop will burn through all 5 attempts without reducing size and the code falls through to `Upload.create_for` and uploads a file that still exceeds `max_image_size_kb`, with no error reported to the user or logged specifically for this scenario, defeating the purpose of the size limit.

findings.title: No tests added for new automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces non-trivial new logic (retry loop with a hardcoded attempt limit, size comparisons, and reliance on `OptimizedImage.downsize`) in `create_upload`, as well as a signature change in `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize`. No spec changes are included to cover the new downsizing loop (e.g., verifying it stops after reaching the limit, after exhausting attempts, or that it is skipped for non-image uploads), leaving this feature and the related method signature change unverified by automated tests.
